prompt.context:
Yermakov Ltd. is a US-based clothing company with stores in 65 countries and 100,000 employees worldwide. The company is in the process of localizing its image by introducing new local lines of fashion through the ongoing acquisition of a dozen high-end boutiques and specialty clothing shops. These acquired businesses exclusively use fair trade sourcing, have close relationships across their supply chain and buyer base, and are much smaller than Yermakov -- the largest acquired company has 120 employees. These employees have deep, specialized knowledge about their industry and are passionate about local fashion and local business.

Yermakov spent the last year working with another consulting firm to analyze and finalize its recent business acquisitions. Now, six months into the post-acquisition era, the company is experiencing growing pains: a large number of employees from the acquired companies declined offers to continue working under the Yermakov umbrella, and customer acquisition and retention in the local fashion market has been lower than expected. This is making long-time Yermakov employees anxious, affecting their day-to-day performance.

Yermakov has approached Deloitte Human Capital for help stabilizing their workforce and communicating a compelling change agenda.
prompt.question: How should Deloitte Human Capital help Yermakov stabilize its workforce and communicate a compelling change agenda following these acquisitions?

clarifying_info.q: Is the other consulting firm still working with the client?
clarifying_info.a: No -- but they do have a point of contact from that team available for communication. Alternatively: Yes -- they are still wrapping up final agreements.

clarifying_info.q: Are most of these 12 acquired companies located in countries where Yermakov already has a business presence?
clarifying_info.a: Yes -- that was part of the criteria for acquisition.

clarifying_info.q: Did staff at the acquired companies have much advance notice of the acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: It differed from company to company, but in general there was usually about a month's notice to employees.

clarifying_info.q: Does Yermakov have an in-house team (apart from acquired company employees) with expertise in local fashion?

framework: Business Issues: Acquisition Management and Workforce Stabilization
Use an Assess -> Implement -> Evaluate structure across three prioritized work streams

Work Stream 1 -- Communication / Change Management: assess change readiness; implement a change management strategy with two-way communication channels (company intranet, all-hands meetings); evaluate via change curve metrics, awareness/adoption rates, and open rates of change communications

Work Stream 2 -- Talent: assess via gap analysis, pulse surveys, and compensation benchmarking; implement talent strategy including competency modeling, career pathing, and rewards/recognition; evaluate via engagement surveys, offer/acceptance rates, and employer ratings

Work Stream 3 -- Culture / Employee Engagement: assess via engagement surveys and stakeholder interviews/workshops; implement engagement strategy balancing Yermakov culture with acquired company sub-cultures; evaluate engagement levels pre- and post-intervention
Other Considerations box: leadership alignment, technology platform integration, stakeholder management, employee benefits and rewards harmonization
Always state assumptions (e.g., engagement dropped post-acquisition; near-term goal is to restore baseline, then improve)
Call out top-line/bottom-line impacts throughout (e.g., retaining acquired employees recoups acquisition investment; improved morale raises productivity)
Review deliverables from the prior consulting firm as an early step

questions.prompt: Why did you prioritize these three work streams?
questions.guidance: Candidate should articulate that Communication/Change Management is most urgent because employees lacked notice and information, creating anxiety. Talent addresses practical gaps in workforce skills and retention. Culture/Engagement addresses the deeper risk of losing the specialized passion and sub-culture that made the boutiques valuable. Candidate should note dependencies: e.g., a talent strategy requires a clear change narrative first.

questions.prompt: If Yermakov can only afford to prioritize one work stream initially, which would you choose and why?
questions.guidance: Strong answers choose Communication/Change Management first. Without a clear, credible change narrative, talent and engagement efforts lack a foundation. The uncertainty felt by both acquired and legacy employees stems primarily from poor communication. This work stream has the broadest immediate impact at relatively low cost.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest risk with the plan you laid out, and how would you minimize it?
questions.guidance: Key risks: further attrition of acquired employees who hold irreplaceable local fashion knowledge; resentment among legacy employees if acquired staff receive perceived preferential treatment; culture homogenization that destroys the differentiation Yermakov paid for. Mitigation: move quickly on communication, involve acquired-company leaders as visible champions, and create integration structures that preserve sub-cultures rather than assimilating them.

questions.prompt: A major challenge is that each acquired company works on a very different technology platform. How would you address this?
questions.guidance: Candidate should add a technology/systems work stream or integrate it into existing ones. Steps: map current platforms across all entities, assess integration complexity and cost, decide on phased migration vs. unified platform, and ensure frontline employees are not burdened with tech disruptions during an already turbulent transition. Framing the tech issue as both a change management and talent challenge earns bonus points.

brainstorming.prompt: Three discussion questions: (1) What is the primary reason Yermakov is experiencing workforce challenges? (2) Why is this such a serious problem for Yermakov? (3) Legacy Yermakov employees are brand ambassadors but know little about local fashion -- how can this be addressed?

categories.name: Root cause of workforce challenges
ideas: Very little advance notice was given to acquired-company employees about the acquisitions
Limited information was provided about how the acquisitions would affect their day-to-day work
Yermakov senior management and HR did not go on-site to formally welcome employees, develop rapport, or hear concerns
Yermakov did not demonstrate that it was acquiring human capital and culture, not just business assets, leading to misalignment and departure

categories.name: Why this is a serious business problem
ideas: People are the most important asset; when undervalued, they underperform and leave
The acquired employees' human talent, local networks, and passion are the most valuable assets Yermakov captured
Failure to retain acquired employees risks losing the core upside of the acquisition investment
Allowing sub-cultures to flourish may be necessary to retain these employees

categories.name: Addressing the local fashion knowledge gap among legacy employees
ideas: Training legacy Yermakov employees on key local fashion talking points and brand story
Incentivizing legacy employees to identify synergies from the acquisitions
Offering professional rotations or temporary assignments at acquired boutiques
Organizing site visits to local fashion subsidiaries
Creating internal knowledge-sharing events or cross-functional teams pairing acquired and legacy staff

recommendation: Yermakov should immediately launch a three-stream Human Capital engagement: (1) a structured change communication program restoring confidence in leadership direction; (2) a talent strategy mapping competency gaps and creating clear career paths for both acquired and legacy employees; and (3) a culture/engagement program that consciously preserves the sub-cultures of acquired companies while building a shared Yermakov identity.

The highest-priority first action is deploying a credible, two-way communication strategy -- including all-hands sessions, a company intranet, and visible senior leader engagement at acquired company sites -- to halt further attrition.
risks: Continued departure of acquired employees who hold irreplaceable local fashion expertise
Technology platform fragmentation adding friction and eroding productivity during the transition
Culture homogenization that strips the differentiated value proposition Yermakov acquired
Legacy employee resentment if change messaging is perceived as favoring acquired staff
next_steps: Review deliverables and data from the prior consulting firm immediately
Conduct change readiness assessments and stakeholder interviews at all acquired companies within the first 30 days
Launch a pulse survey across both legacy and acquired employee bases to establish an engagement baseline
Develop a competency model reflecting the combined Yermakov-plus-local-fashion workforce needs
Design a rewards and recognition strategy that acknowledges both sets of cultural values
Incorporate relevant market trends (gig economy, millennial workforce expectations) into the long-term talent roadmap
